description: Committee considered widening 51st Street and Millar Avenue to six lanes.
This would restrict left turns for adjacent businesses.
The $6.24 million project is currently unfunded.

chips.text: Defeated
1 for, 5 against
Mayor Block empathized with businesses not feeling heard, supported deferral.
Adjacent businesses like Tim Hortons, McDonald's would lose left-turn access.
Staff confirmed 'impact on businesses' was a criteria, despite report typo.
Traffic loss to businesses from restricted access could not be forecasted.
Adjacent businesses opposed Option C due to restricted access and parking loss.
Councillors cited business concerns, feeling unheard, and removed criteria for opposition.
City has ability to expropriate land if owners do not sell.
Project would require removal of city and private trees.

description: Committee deferred decision on Millar Avenue active transportation pathways.
It requested staff engage businesses about parking loss and solutions.
The $8.47 million project is currently unfunded.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor Dunner questioned the project's impact on businesses and parking loss.
Businesses on Millar Avenue will lose parking on public right-of-way.
Councillor Dunner questioned if engagement process was unduly impacted by special interest groups.
Some businesses opposed the project due to parking loss and economic impact.
City Solicitor stated businesses never had explicit permission to use right-of-way for parking.
Staff cited equity as a reason for pathways on both sides of arterial roads.
Project requires removal of 197 trees, with replanting planned.

description: Committee recommends detailed design for 8th Street overpass.
Overpass addresses future traffic growth at rail crossing.
Developer contributions will fund design and construction.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Staff confirmed West Road access from 8th Street will close.
Residents near 8th Street and Breyerwood will experience noise impacts.
Public engagement showed broad support for overpass with noise mitigation requests.
Sound walls are included in the overpass budget for noise reduction.

5 for, 0 against

description: City improves fleet services through continuous improvement.

Administration promises to report quantifiable benefits and savings in future reports.
